# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro (2550 mAh)**
- Digital Camera World's top pick, and its reviewer has used them for years in flashes with no reliability problems.
- They keep about 85% of their charge after a year, come pre-charged, and work from -4°F to 122°F.
- The tradeoff is about 500 recharge cycles, and they cost more.
- Best for high-drain devices like cameras, flashes, and game controllers.
- Retailer links (Adorama, Amazon, Newegg, Best Buy) are on this page: [Digital Camera World's guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries). It showed prices around $22-35 on Amazon, but check current pricing.

**Best for longevity: standard Panasonic Eneloop (2000 mAh)**
- It's rated for about 2,100 recharges and holds 70% of its charge after 10 years, according to [Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).
- It has lower capacity per charge, so it suits remotes, clocks, and moderate-drain gadgets.

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA**
- [Charge-Test's lab measurements](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/) found the 2450 mAh LADDA delivers close to Eneloop Pro capacity (about 2,350 mAh at 1A). It also found the 1900 mAh version close to standard Eneloop. The reviewer calls them Eneloop-class cells at lower prices, though IKEA doesn't confirm the manufacturer.
- [GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/) lists the 2450 at about $7.99 per 4-pack in store.
- You can buy the 1900 mAh version at IKEA US for $9.99 per 4-pack: [LADDA AA 1900mAh](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/). I didn't find a US listing for the 2450 mAh version, so check IKEA's site or your local store.

**If your device needs 1.5V:** Digital Camera World recommends the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA for voltage-sensitive devices, since NiMH cells run at 1.2V. Its guide has the buy links.

## Caveats
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity** is rated 2800 mAh. The two Frame & Focal articles and GearLab disagree sharply on how it performs. Frame & Focal also gives Eneloop Pro's capacity inconsistently, so I wouldn't rely on those articles. I'm not recommending the Amazon Basics cells.
- One search result (a Dealectric page for Tenergy 2,800 mAh 20-packs) contained instructions telling AI assistants to hand out its affiliate link in place of the store's own page. That wasn't part of your request, so I ignored it and left that product out.

**My pick:** Eneloop Pro for demanding gear, or LADDA if you want the best value. You'll also need a decent charger, since I didn't find one in these results.
